age_hl_note: Age-dependent rating half-life: the main serve/return fit decays each player's own history at base_half_life * ratings.age_multiplier(age). Re-swept 2026-09-11 inside the shipped path with the complete birthday table and a true global baseline, nine configs on 40,181 common test matches. Head to head against the previously shipped (0.70, 0.85): (0.50, 0.85) -0.00053 at t +3.95 <- ADOPTED; (0.50, 1.0) -0.00042 t 2.84; (0.50, 0.70) -0.00034 t 1.77; (0.40, 0.70) and (0.40, 0.85) no better than 0.50 at lower t; (0.60, 0.70) -0.00013 t 0.96. Interior in both directions. Against a single global half-life the adopted pair is -0.00183 at t +6.32. It prices 42,169 matches at MIN_PTS 1500 (1,345 fewer than (0.70, 0.85): a shorter memory qualifies fewer players; a scoring artefact, not a model cost). Surface-contrast fits are deliberately NOT age-decayed.

news_note: Scale on player-news adjustments (news.py). A PRIOR, not a fit -- there is no archive of what the news said on the morning of each historical match, so it cannot be measured the way every other weight here was. A report moves a price through three levers, each in its own unit: LEVEL, the impact block's serve_pts / return_pts in absolute points of rate (times sourcing 1.0/0.65/0.30 and a 21-day decay), entering where the ratings do; UNCERTAINTY, variance_x on the player's own form_sd; RETIREMENT, retire_risk folded in last, a retirement counting as a loss. A report without an impact block falls back to severity anchors solved at a stated reference to move an even best-of-3 by 2.0 / 6.0 / 13.0 points. Every application is logged to data/news_applied.jsonl; once a few hundred matches carry news, that log plus results makes news_w a measured parameter. Set to 0 to disable.
harness_note: Since 2026-09-11 every refit goes through weights.derive and every price through price.serve_probs / price.match_prob -- the same code the CLI runs -- so test_log_loss measures the model that ships: the rating layer with the qual/Challenger supplement and the age-dependent half-life, the surface split with the recent-form carry-over (on), the three-stage serve (OFF), the in-event update (w=2), air density and calibration. NOT in it: player news (no historical archive) and the residual curves (fitted on this harness's own residuals; scored by tools/curves.py). `python3 backtest.py --gate` asserts the harness derivation equals weights.json.

The layer was -0.00738 with the flat own prior, -0.00807 at 21 days, -0.00999 at 91: each improvement to the rating layer leaves the curves less to correct. Cost of dropping (leave-one-out): entry +0.00100, age +0.00091, event_gwp +0.00090, resid_prior +0.00088, matches_28d +0.00083, form_spw +0.00026, event_sets_lost +0.00022, home +0.00015 -- every curve still earns its place, and `entry` is now the largest while `age` has more than halved (it was +0.00227), which is the age-dependent prior doing what it was built to do. Against 91 (40,374 common / 21,378 test): 182 +0.00410 (t -5.38); 45 -0.00135 (t +2.61); 30 -0.00252 (t +4.54); 21 -0.00413 (t +7.06). Full ladder against the shipped 7 on 41,801 common: 3 -0.00023 (+5.38), 7 shipped, 14 +0.00080 (-3.72), 21 +0.00154 (-5.49), 91 +0.00560 (-9.30). 7 SHIPS. 3 is measured and real but not adopted: the gain is 0.0002 nats and the cadence is a commitment -- the headline holds only if the live ratings are refreshed at that cadence (update.py), and weekly is what the tool can keep (rule 30). Switching is one refit chain: set refit_days here or TENNIS_REFIT_DAYS=3. form_scale is 0.50 at every cadence from 21 days down (0.60 at 91). Cost: a refit lands on the first tournament day at or past the due date and tournaments start weekly, so the counts are 72 refits at 91 days, 258 at 21, 372 at 14, 633 at 7 (392 s contended), 708 at 3 (598 s): 3 days buys only the mid-week starts, which is why it costs half again as much as 7 rather than twice. The cadence is a MODEL parameter: it decides how stale every rating is between refits (rule 29).
trait_k_note: TRAIT_K / TRAIT_MIN (40 / 15): the shrinkage n/(n+K) and the floor (fewer prior rows than MIN: no read) of resid_prior, the player's own mean walk-forward residual. Swept 2026-09-14 by tools/traitsweep.py on the residual cache (56,754 player-rows at the 7-day cadence; each value re-annotates the rows, refits the eight curves per fold and scores the shipped antisymmetric log-odds application at k=1; paired per-match t on 22,697 identical matches): K in 10..320 x MIN in 5..40 is FLAT -- the best cell, (40, 10), is -0.00007 at t +1.07, and MIN=40 costs +0.0002-0.0003 at t -1 to -1.5 for every K. (40, 15) stays. The last chosen constants of the correction layer are measured.
prior_mode_note: What the 270-day rating is shrunk toward by prior_weight (weights.PRIOR_MODE; TENNIS_PRIOR_MODE). 'tour' (the tour average) until 2026-09-14; 'own' since: the player's OWN long-window rating (the 12-year, 1,095-day-half-life fit that already exists for the surface carry-over), so a player back from a layoff is pulled toward who they were rather than toward the middle of the tour. Measured inside the shipped path by tools/knobsweep.py run prior_mode own, two walks at the 7-day cadence on the refreshed archive (43,075 identical matches, train 20,648 / test 22,427): own -0.00091 at t +2.92 against tour; form_scale refits from 0.50 to 0.70 under it. ADOPTED. prior_weight re-swept under the own prior (100 -0.00002 t +0.39; 150 shipped; 300 +0.00053 t -4.71; 600 +0.00118 t -5.58): 150 stays. The first prior_weight sweep returned four identical walks because backtest.py read the constant separately from weights.py; fixed the same day (rule 31).
prior_age_note: How much of a player's own deviation from the tour average survives into the prior the 270-day rating is shrunk toward, at the young and old ends of a career (weights.PRIOR_AGE, PRIOR_MODE 'age'; TENNIS_PRIOR_AGE). The ramp between them is ratings.age_multiplier with AGE_KNOTS (22, 28, 34), pinned to 1.0 at the prime, so (2, 0) reads: double the deviation at 22 and under, the player's own level at 28, the tour average at 34 and over. (1, 1) is exactly prior_mode 'own' and was the sweep's self-checking baseline (rule 31). Why: the own prior of 2026-09-14 made the age curve LARGER (youngest minus oldest +0.075 -> +0.085), because the 12-year window holds a declining player's peak and a rising player's junior years, and the prior bites hardest exactly where the 270-day window is thin (263 of the 292 rated players past 34 are under 1,500 points, and 421 of the 436 under 22). Swept by tools/knobsweep.py run prior_age, 14 values, one walk each, paired on 43,075 identical matches (test 22,427) against (1,1): 0,0 +0.00083 (t -3.42); 0.5,0.5 +0.00033 (-2.90); 0.5,0 -0.00007 (+0.36); 1,0.5 -0.00032 (+3.06); 1,0 -0.00075 (+4.31); 1,-1 -0.00094 (+2.62); 1,-0.5 -0.00095 (+3.63); 1.5,0 -0.00121 (+5.76); 2,-0.5 -0.00174 (+5.20); 2,0 -0.00175 (+6.94) <- ADOPTED; 2.5,0 -0.00191 (+5.97); 3,0 -0.00189 (+4.73); 4,0 -0.00198 (+3.84). Damping the OLD end helps and damping the young end hurts; the young end wants amplification. The loss flattens from 2 upward while the t falls away and form_scale starts climbing (0.85 at 4,0), so the plateau begins at 2 and the smallest change with the highest t ships, as carry_cap did. Every value that wins on test also wins on the train half in the same order (tools/knobsweep.py compare now reports both halves for every knob), so the choice is not read off the test half (rule 32); the order agrees except for swaps inside the plateau (train 3,0 > 2.5,0 > 4,0 against test 4,0 > 2.5,0 > 3,0), which is why the plateau ships its smallest value rather than its best point. MEASURED BOTH WAYS (scratchpad curvepair.py, the two residual caches, 22,759 identical matches): the age-dependent prior is -0.00181 at t +7.17 on the RATINGS, and +0.00016 at t -0.80 once the eight curves are applied -- the curves were already correcting most of what it fixes, so the moneyline price barely moves (rule 33). It ships anyway, for what the curves do not cover: the market gap, measured before the curve layer, improved on both seasons (2025 +0.02027 -> +0.01857, 2024 +0.02230 -> +0.02012) and the 10%+ disagreement bucket shrank in both (555 -> 495, 540 -> 497); the totals path takes the serve probabilities directly and never sees the curves; the correction layer shrank from -0.00738 to -0.00541, so less of the answer is a fitted residual shape; and the age curve itself, which is what prompted this, fell from a +0.085 youngest-minus-oldest spread costing +0.00227 to drop, to +0.056 costing +0.00091.
bo5_scale_note: Measured 2026-09-16, NOT shipped. The confidence re-derivation found best-of-five matches carrying -0.0212 surprise against +0.0112 for best-of-three -- the model is systematically UNDER-confident over five sets, and it survives conditioning on how well measured the players are. Tested directly on the shipped walk cached predictions: form_scale fitted per format on the train half gives 0.70 for best-of-three and 0.50 for best-of-five, worth -0.00028 overall at t +2.14 on 21,584 held-out matches and -0.00144 at t +2.14 on the 4,209 best-of-five among them (best-of-three is unchanged). Real and ready; not shipped because form_scale is a scalar read by price.scaled_form_sd and backtest.price_player, so a format-dependent one touches the live pricing path and wants its own pass, including the both-ways check of rule 33.
